newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong ponders source of stock rally funds.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong ponders source of stock rally funds.

text.p: Everybody from punters to strategists in Hong Kong is trying to figure out the source of funds driving the Hang Seng index to spectacular record highs.

Theories abound. The switching of funds among Asian markets, a heady gush of enthusiasm from mainland Chinese investors or sudden foreign inflows from Japan, the United States and Europe -- all take the credit for Hong Kong's stock market fervour.

Hong Kong's key index of 33 blue chip stocks has skyrocketed 1,645 points or 15 percent since early September's level of 10,957, reaching another record intraday high on Wednesday of 12,602, up 111 points from Tuesday's close. On Wednesday, the Hang Seng index closed 94.52 points lower at 12,396.18.
The variety of views suggests nobody can safely pinpoint a primary driving force in the rally.
"None of these opinions are contradictory. It is a combination of all of them," said Daniel Widdicombe, managing director at Bear Stearns Asia Ltd.

Widdicombe cited specific orders to back up his view that U.S. funds are entering Hong Kong on fears that U.S. earnings growth has peaked and that the Dow Jones Industrial Average has topped out following its recent high of 6,043.92.
